slot.brief: Circuit diagram with a silicon diode in series with a resistor and a DC source; using a constant forward voltage drop model, find the circuit current and power dissipated in the diode or resistor.

stem: In the circuit shown, assume the silicon diode has a constant forward voltage drop of $0.70\ \text{V}$. What power is dissipated in the diode?

verdicts.working: The diode is forward-biased. The current is $(10-0.70)/1.0\,\text{k}\Omega=9.3\,\text{mA}$, so its power is $0.70\times9.3\,\text{mA}=6.51\,\text{mW}$.

working:
$I=\dfrac{10-0.70}{1.0\times10^3}=9.3\times10^{-3}\ \text{A}$. $P_D=V_DI=0.70(9.3\times10^{-3})=6.51\times10^{-3}\ \text{W}=6.51\ \text{mW}$.

Independent check: The diode is forward-biased. The current is $(10-0.70)/1.0\,\text{k}\Omega=9.3\,\text{mA}$, so its power is $0.70\times9.3\,\text{mA}=6.51\,\text{mW}$.

draft.stem: In the circuit shown, assume the silicon diode has a constant forward voltage drop of $0.70\ \text{V}$. What power is dissipated in the diode?

figure.description: Draw one closed rectangular series loop. On the left vertical branch, draw a DC source labeled 10 V, with its positive terminal at the top and negative terminal at the bottom. On the top branch, draw a resistor labeled 1.0 kΩ. On the right branch, draw a diode with its anode at the top (connected to the resistor) and its cathode bar at the bottom. Connect the diode’s lower terminal directly to the source’s negative terminal with a wire. Show a clockwise conventional-current arrow.

draft.distractor_notes: A: uses a $1.0\ \text{V}$ drop to calculate the current. C: calculates the current as $10\ \text{mA}$ without subtracting the diode drop. D: uses the source voltage instead of the diode drop to calculate diode power.
